findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before being replaced
findings.description:
The new guard `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always false for the real processes.
- **Why:** they are created with `self.mp_context.Process` from `get_context("spawn")` (line 53, 105), which is `SpawnProcess`. In CPython, `SpawnProcess` and `multiprocessing.Process` are sibling subclasses of `BaseProcess`, not parent and child. The file's own annotation on line 68 says `SpawnProcess`.
- **Regression:** the base code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now, on `cause = "hang"`, `kill()` is skipped and line 259 spawns a replacement for the same shards while the hung process stays alive.
- **Impact:** if the old process recovers, two flushers work the same Redis queues and can produce duplicate segments to `buffered-segments`. Up to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` processes can leak per slot.
- **Fix:** check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)`, or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: `join()` never terminates processes and skips the rest once the deadline passes
findings.description:
- **Same `isinstance` problem:** line 346 uses the same always-false check, so `process.terminate()` is never reached. This existed in the base for one process; the diff copies it into the loop.
- **New early exit:** the `break` at line 341 leaves the loop when the deadline expires. Even with the check fixed, every process after that point would be neither waited on nor terminated.
- **Impact:** on a rebalance the parent keeps running, so a stuck flusher survives alongside those created for the next assignment.
- **Fix:** wait against the shared deadline, then terminate all remaining processes in a separate pass. `process_index` is unused in this loop.

findings.title: Added `time.sleep(0.1)` in `test_basic` is a no-op
findings.description: `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately. The comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" is therefore untrue. The race between the flusher thread seeing the new drift and `step.join()` setting `stopped` is still open, so `(msg,) = messages` can flake. `test_flusher.py:2` avoids this by binding `from time import sleep` before the patch; do the same here or poll for `messages` with a deadline.

findings.title: New test asserts internal state only; restart and multi-process paths are untested
findings.description:
- **What it checks:** `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts only on `flusher.processes`, `max_processes`, `num_processes` and the size of `process_to_shards_map`. It submits no spans, so it does not show that segments from all four shards are flushed when processes share shards.
- **What nothing checks:** `_ensure_processes_alive` (dead/hang detection, per-process restart counter, the `RuntimeError` threshold) and the multi-process `join()`.
- **Why the FAIL slipped through:** both tests pass `produce_to_pipe`, which selects `threading.Thread`, so the `SpawnProcess` branch is never exercised.
- **Minor:** `commits` and `add_commit` in the new test are unused boilerplate.

findings.title: Parent queries Redis once per flusher process for identical data
findings.description:
- **Memory check:** `submit()` calls `get_memory_info()` on every entry in `self.buffers`. That call runs `INFO` on the whole span-buffer cluster regardless of the buffer's shards (`src/sentry/processing/backpressure/memory.py:82-105`).
- **Effect:** with N flusher processes, the same cluster is polled N times per `submit()`. `used` and `available` are both inflated N-fold, so the ratio is unchanged and the extra round trips buy nothing.
- **Queue sizes:** `record_stored_segments()` at lines 269-270 likewise becomes N pipelines instead of one.
- **Fix:** keep the `buffer` passed to `__init__` (the diff drops `self.buffer`) and use it for both calls. `self.buffers` then has no purpose in the parent.

findings.title: `--flusher-processes` accepts zero and negative values
findings.description:
- **Negative:** the option is `type=int` with no range. With `--flusher-processes -1`, `num_processes` becomes `-1` at `flusher.py:60`, the map is empty, and `i % -1 == 0` raises `KeyError` at line 66 on partition assignment.
- **Zero:** `max_processes or len(...)` at line 51 treats `0` as "one per shard", the opposite of what the operator typed.
- **Fix:** use `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

findings.title: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` and `if not process`
findings.description: `_create_process_for_shard` has no callers anywhere in the repo; the restart path calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. The `if not process: continue` guard at lines 222-223 cannot trigger, since `self.processes` only ever holds started process or thread objects. Remove both.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys and values for shards
findings.description:
- **Key drift:** `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the key `shards`, while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` (lines 185, 195) use `shard`.
- **Value drift:** in `main` the value is a comma-joined list such as `"0,2"`; `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) tags `shard` with a single int; `SpansBuffer` uses `shard_i` for the same concept (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:372`, `447`).
- **Impact:** dashboards cannot group across these.
- **Fix:** pick one key, and use a different one (e.g. a process index) where the value is a group of shards.

findings.title: Docstring contradicts the actual process model
findings.description:
- **Process model:** the class docstring says "Creates one process per shard", but processes are capped by `max_processes` with shards assigned round-robin, and the CLI default is 1 process for all shards.
- **Parameters:** `max_processes` is undocumented, and the existing `:param topic:` refers to a parameter that does not exist.
- **Defaults:** the constructor default (`None`, one per shard) differs from the CLI default (`1`); say so explicitly.
- **Stale comments:** line 178 ("for all shards") and line 235 ("Check if any shard…") describe per-shard logic the code does not have.

findings.title: `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` now applies per flusher process
findings.description: Each process gets its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`, and `flush_segments` divides `max-flush-segments` by `len(self.assigned_shards)` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384`). The cap therefore applies per process: total segments per cycle, and the `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure threshold, scale with `--flusher-processes`. Nothing changes at the default of 1, but operators raising the flag should know.

findings.title: Shard partitioning and factory/CLI plumbing
findings.description:
- **Plumbing:** `flusher_processes` flows from the click option through `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`.
- **Partitioning:** the round-robin split in `flusher.py:61-66` puts each assigned shard in exactly one process.
- **Restart loop:** replacing `self.processes[process_index]` while iterating in `_ensure_processes_alive` does not change the dict's size, so it is safe.
- **Shared state:** `stopped` and `current_drift` are correctly shared across processes; health and backpressure values are per process.
